title: Phone Letter Combinations
statement:
Given digits typed on a phone keypad, list every letter string they could spell.

Contract
- The keypad letters are `2` abc, `3` def, `4` ghi, `5` jkl, `6` mno, `7` pqrs, `8` tuv, `9` wxyz.
- `digits` is a non-null string. It may be empty, in which case the result is an empty list (not a list holding an empty string).
- Return every string that picks one letter for each digit in order. A string of k digits yields the product of the letter counts of its digits.
- Throw `IllegalArgumentException` if `digits` contains any character other than `2` to `9`. The order of the results does not matter.

Examples
- `combinations("23")` returns `["ad", "ae", "af", "bd", "be", "bf", "cd", "ce", "cf"]` in any order.
- `combinations("7")` returns `["p", "q", "r", "s"]`.
- `combinations("")` returns `[]`.
hints: Store the letters for each digit in a lookup table, then build the answer one digit at a time.

Recurse over the digit positions with a shared character buffer: at position i, try each letter of digit i, recurse to i + 1, and when the buffer has one letter per digit emit it as a string. Validate the digits before generating anything.

Reuse one buffer rather than concatenating strings at every level. The number of results is exponential in the number of digits; the probe measures a batch of n calls on the fixed input "234" (27 results each), so the work grows linearly in n. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for that batch, and O(k * 4^k) per call in general.
